LONDON -- The death toll from last week's flash flooding disaster in the Nepal-Tibet border region rose to at least 955 people as of Monday, according to the latest updates from Nepali and Chinese officials, with more than 4,400 people reported missing.

At least 939 bodies had been recovered in Nepal as of Monday, the Nepal National Disaster Management Authority said in a post to X. At least 3,925 people were listed missing, the authority said, marking a significant jump on Sunday's figure.

China's state-run Xinhua News Agency, meanwhile, said that at least 16 people had been confirmed killed on the Tibetan side of the border. Xinhua reported that another 546 people were still missing.

In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, a drone carries cargo overhead as search and rescue operations are underway at the mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County, southwestern China's Tibet Autonomous Region, on Aug. 29, 2026. Jiang Fan/Xinhua via AP

The missing count declined from initial reports on Monday morning local time due to a combination of finding more bodies, rescuing more people and families reporting they had found missing relatives, an official with Nepal's National Disaster Management Authority told ABC News.

The State Department is aware of 80 Americans who are unaccounted for in Nepal as of Monday morning, and 13 U.S. citizens have made their way to safety in Nepal, according to a State Department spokesperson.

"Our priority is the safety and security of the American people. As you mentioned, the remoteness of this location makes getting reliable information difficult. But our dedication remains," State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott told ABC News' Martha Raddatz on "This Week" on Sunday.

Residents carry their belongings salvaged from their damaged homes filled with mud and debris in Devighat, in Nepal's Nuwakot district, on Aug. 29, 2026, following the Aug. 26 flash floods. Rajesh Kumar Singh/AP Photo

"We have activated from the State Department $3.6 million in emergency humanitarian assistance that includes up to three months of emergency food for up to 10,000 flood-affected households," he said.

A United Nations assessment determined that some 65,000 people require emergency water, sanitation and hygiene support, and more than 22,000 children need protection, a United Nations spokesperson said on Monday.

The flooding occurred in the northern Rasuwa district along the border with Tibet at around 8:40 a.m. local time Wednesday, authorities said. The flooding inundated areas along the Trishuli River, burying buildings and damaging bridges and roadways.

The wall of ice, water and debris that descended from the mountains on the frontier between Nepal and Tibet caused destruction at least 62 miles downriver into Nepal, an ABC News analysis of verified video and satellite images shows.

This graphic shows destruction along the path of a landslide and subsequent flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border. Felt Maps/ABC News

The flood was reportedly triggered by a landslide about 12 miles northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border post along the frontier, according to Nepali officials.

A 5.2-magnitude landslide was registered in Nepal on Wednesday, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

The initial location of the glacier was a cliff about 16,000 feet high. The debris avalanche, or landslide, slid down 6,000 feet on the slope, the USGS said.

Among the missing are hundreds of workers in hydro project tunnels, underground passages that facilitate the movement of water from hydro projects. In the last three days, 301 people have been rescued from the tunnels, according to Nepal's National Disaster Management Authority.

Video footage released by Nepal's Prime Minister's Office shows mud-covered people being dragged out of the tunnels to safety. Tunnel search-and-rescue operations are ongoing.

Rescuers carry bodies of flash flood victims for a mass burial in Chitwan, Nepal, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (AP Photo/Nisha Shrestha) The Associated Press

On Monday, the U.S. Embassy in Kathmandu warned Americans against all travel to the affected region, noting "flood damage, disrupted transportation and communications, search-and-rescue and recovery operations, and the risk of additional flooding and landslides."

The embassy also urged Americans to "exercise increased caution in Nepal due to civil unrest. Some areas have increased risk."

ABC News' Victoria Beaule contributed to this report.

title: The Papers: '45m Brits in drought' and a 'Not-so-small boats crisis'
author: Watch Our Pick Of Standout Clips Across The Bbc
content:
Many of the papers lead on the arrival of a record 230 migrants on a single 49ft dinghy. The Daily Mail, external notes the number is more than the capacity of a Boeing-737 and says the small boats crisis has become a "big boats crisis". The Sun, external takes a similar approach with its headline, "not-so-small boats crisis". It says the crossing will cost taxpayers £25m. The Daily Telegraph, external carries a warning from the French lifeboat service, which says there is "no limit" to the number of migrants people smugglers will put on board the giant dinghies.

Andy Burnham's call for the justice secretary to draw up plans to exclude PC Harper's killers from the prison early release scheme leads the Times, external. A government source is quoted in the report, saying the prime minister never accepted that Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers should walk free.

The Daily Mirror, external reports on the drought conditions for most of Britain under the headline, "high and dry". The paper says 45 million people are now in drought areas. The Guardian, external says firefighters have warned they aren't properly equipped to deal with what they call an "unprecedented" surge in wildfires as a result of the dry conditions. According to the report, the Fire Brigades Union says ensuring crews are prepared to tackle the rising threat should be a "national priority".

The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, has told the Daily Express, external that Andy Burnham needs to rule out further tax rises to fund his new policies. Writing in the paper, she says the prime minister and his new chancellor, John Healey, face a "tricky test" in the Budget. In response, Labour says it will focus on problem solving, not point scoring.

The Financial Times, external leads on what it calls one of Wall Street's most ambitious lending efforts. It says some of the largest financial groups are working on a five hundred billion dollar package with the artificial intelligence firm, Nvidia, to invest in AI data centres.

"You'll never deliver alone" reads the Daily Star's, external headline with the paper reporting on the Amazon founder, Jeff Bezos, nearing a deal to buy a stake in Liverpool football club. Its front page features a picture of a Liverpool player with the billionaire's face edited on.

title: The Papers: 'Britons lost in Nepal flood' and 'Regal had landed'
author: Watch Our Pick Of Standout Clips Across The Bbc
content:
The front page of the Times, external charts the destruction at the Nepal-Tibet border with images of people running for their lives as mud, water and debris engulf a building.

The Daily Mail describes, external the disaster as an "apocalyptic mudslide" that "wiped out everything in its path". The paper says witnesses thought they were seeing explosions caused by a military invasion, as clouds of debris were thrown up into the air.

The i Paper, external on Meta's decision to pay billions of dollars to settle claims - which it denies - that Facebook and Instagram harmed children. The paper notes the firm's agreement to make apps safer for young people will not apply to the UK.

The Guardian's analysis, external calls the introduction of default protections for teens "a major concession", that "sets a precedent others in the tech industry are likely to follow".

"Well that's told 'em", quips the Sun's columnist, external, Colin Robertson, who points out the cost of the settlement represents just over one per cent of Meta's $1.4 trillion value.

The Daily Telegraph says, external it understands that Germany is in talks to invest in Britain's nuclear deterrent, as part of efforts to reduce Europe's reliance on the US.

The paper says military planners in Berlin believe they could contribute air defences to key locations, such as the base in Faslane that houses submarines armed with the UK's Trident missiles.

Andy Burnham has spoken the Financial Times, external in what it describes as his "most pro-business interview since becoming prime minister".

He tells the FT he's "acutely conscious of how hard the operating environment is for businesses", but declines to say whether taxes on companies would rise in the upcoming Budget.

The coverage of the outpouring of affection for the late queen of country, Dolly Parton, spills into a second day, with jourrnalists who were lucky enough to interview her setting out their memories.

In the Daily Express, external, Paul Sexton describes her as "side-splittingly funny" and "bigger than country music itself". The Daily Mirror's, external Tom Bryant recalls how she made him feel "at the centre of her world, despite her enormous fame".
